comparison: Both OpenEval and peer reviewers strongly support the gradient identification findings (C31-C44). OpenEval emphasizes robust quantification and variance explained across modalities, while peer reviewers praise the 'comprehensive combination of multimodal data' and 'solid evidence with multimodal validation.' Both evaluations are aligned in finding these claims well-supported.

Both evaluations support claims C45-C46 regarding poor correspondence between gradients and discrete nuclear boundaries. OpenEval focuses on quantitative Dice coefficients, while peer reviewers accept that organization is 'better captured by continuous gradients' rather than discrete subdivisions. Both also reference the reconciliation claims (C95-C98) covered in peer R2.

Both strongly support the replication principle findings (C47-C52). OpenEval emphasizes statistical evidence with high correlations and spatial autocorrelation corrections. Peer reviewers explicitly acknowledge this as offering 'robust formal evidence of this organizational principle in the human brain.' Both note the contrast with structural connectivity (C54). Peer R3 also includes related dorso-ventral axis claims (C55-C57) and interpretation claims (C103-C105).

Both support the dorso-ventral organizational axis findings (C55-C69). OpenEval highlights convergent multimodal evidence and mechanistic insights from receptor patterns. Peer reviewers praise the 'comprehensive combination of multimodal data' and note the study 'reveals stronger associations between pulvinar-cortical connectivity to specific functional networks and the spatial distribution of markers.' Both evaluations align on the strength of receptor-connectivity correlations.

Both support the medio-lateral organizational axis findings (C70-C82). OpenEval emphasizes strong correlations and specific receptor patterns complementing the dorso-ventral axis. Peer reviewers accept these as part of the overall 'thorough characterization' with 'solid' evidence, without raising specific concerns about these secondary gradient relationships.

Perfect agreement on reliability and reproducibility evidence (C83-C89). OpenEval provides detailed assessment of split-half, test-retest, and cross-dataset validation metrics. Peer reviewers explicitly acknowledged that 'the authors performed various robustness checks, answering my concerns' during revision. Both evaluations strongly support these validation findings.

Both support the quality control findings (C90-C91) addressing SNR confounds. OpenEval notes weak correlations suggest findings are not SNR-driven but cautions about GFC3. Peer reviewers accepted this as part of robustness checks performed in revision. Both evaluations view this as strengthening confidence in the results.

Both support claims C92-C98 about reconciling continuous and discrete organization. OpenEval emphasizes how gradients improve upon previous methodological approaches and reconcile different organizational views. Peer R2 explicitly accepts that organization is 'better captured by continuous gradients' and that the finding reconciles continuous representations with discrete specialization.

Both support contextualization within theoretical frameworks (C99-C105). OpenEval emphasizes how findings extend primate work to humans with strong correlational evidence. Peer R3 acknowledges the study 'offers robust formal evidence of this organizational principle' and accepts the replication principle interpretation without challenge.

Overlap on interpretation claims (C102). OpenEval supports contextualization within established frameworks. Peer R8 accepts these interpretive findings as part of the overall characterization, noting consistency with prior primate work (Shipp's model) was not challenged.

Both support functional significance interpretations (C106-C111, with overlap on C107-C108). OpenEval finds these well-supported by correlation data and consistent with cited literature. Peer R8 accepts these as providing 'a more nuanced understanding of the overarching organizational principles' without challenge.

OpenEval rates temporal dynamics claims (C112-C115) as UNCERTAIN, noting these are speculative extensions beyond current data since the study did not measure temporal dynamics. No corresponding peer review evaluation was found for these specific claims.

Both support contextualization within broader thalamic literature (C116-C122, with overlap on C119, C122). OpenEval finds interpretations well-supported by data and citations. Peer R8 accepts these as part of the overall characterization, noting the work provides useful understanding of organizational principles.

Both support molecular findings and receptor-connectivity correlations (C123-C131, with overlap on C126-C127). OpenEval emphasizes alignment between connectivity and receptor gradients with appropriate caution about resolution. Peer R4 praises the multimodal data combination and notes stronger associations between connectivity and molecular markers.

Overlap on molecular interpretation claim C125. OpenEval supports molecular findings in context of prior literature. Peer R8 accepts these interpretations as part of the thorough characterization without raising concerns.

Both support functional interpretation of molecular findings (C132-C137, with overlap on C132). OpenEval finds interpretations well-supported with appropriate citations. Peer R4 accepts these as part of the comprehensive multimodal characterization showing associations between connectivity and molecular markers.

Divergence on clinical applications (C138-C146, with overlap on C138, C143-C144). OpenEval rates these as UNCERTAIN, noting they are largely speculative extensions representing future directions rather than established applications. Peer R12 also expresses UNCERTAINTY, noting 'there remains an opportunity for a more fully integrated interpretation' and the manuscript 'falls short in presenting the authors' unique perspectives on integrating the diverse biological principles.' Both evaluations agree these translational claims need stronger development.

Perfect agreement on methodological limitations (C147-C154). OpenEval finds the acknowledgment honest and appropriate, noting limitations are inherent to current technology. Peer R10 explicitly acknowledges resolution limitations, stating 'even higher-resolution imaging data would have strengthened the study' while accepting current resolution meets standards. Both evaluations view the transparent discussion of limitations positively.

Both support summary conclusions (C155-C159, with strong overlap on C155-C158). OpenEval finds conclusions well-supported by convergent multimodal evidence. Peer R11 accepts these as supported, describing the characterization as 'useful' with 'solid' evidence and 'thorough characterization of the functional neuroanatomy.' Both evaluations align on the integrative nature of these conclusions.

Overlap on unified framework claim C159. OpenEval supports this as appropriately qualified potential application. Peer R12 expresses some uncertainty about integration, noting opportunity for 'more fully integrated interpretation,' suggesting this framework claim could be strengthened.

Both address structural connectivity findings (C54). OpenEval notes the contrast with functional connectivity strengthens specificity of functional findings. Peer R9 accepts the limitation that structural connectivity did not replicate functional results, noting this is 'likely due to the inherent disproportion between pulvinar-cortical connections and the whole-brain connectome' and is transparently reported.

Overlap on structural gradient claims C65-C66. OpenEval supports these as part of convergent multimodal evidence for dorso-ventral axis. Peer R9 accepts the finding while acknowledging structural connectivity limitations compared to functional connectivity.

OpenEval supports background claims C1-C2, C10-C11 as well-established anatomical facts providing appropriate context. No specific peer review evaluation was found addressing these background claims separately.
OpenEval supports rationale and knowledge gap claims C3-C6 as establishing study motivation. No specific peer review evaluation was found addressing these motivational claims separately.

OpenEval supports literature summary claims C12-C20 as accurately representing prior work and establishing theoretical framework. No specific peer review evaluation was found addressing these literature review claims separately.

OpenEval supports claims C21-C24 describing limitations of prior research and justifying the gradient-based approach. No specific peer review evaluation was found addressing these methodological justification claims separately.

OpenEval supports methodological background claims C25-C30 on gradient mapping and pulvinar-specific focus. No specific peer review evaluation was found addressing these methodological background claims separately.

Peer R1 includes claims C7-C8 not separately evaluated by OpenEval. These appear to be additional background or contextual claims that peer reviewers grouped with the main gradient findings (C31-C44).
